subject: Banking
title: Credit Cards Decoded
description: A fast breakdown of Credit Cards Decoded for builders.

hook.text: A credit card can be a free 25-day loan or a 24% trap depending on whether you carry the balance.

buildup.text: Cards offer a grace period of 21-25 days. Pay the full balance and interest is zero.

discovery.text: Minimum payments are designed to maximize interest. Paying only the minimum on $5,000 takes 22 years and costs $7,000.

twist.text: The rewards system is funded by interchange fees charged to merchants, which raise prices for everyone.

climax.text: Credit cards reward discipline and punish debt. The same product is free for some and devastating for others.

punchline.text: Pay in full: free money. Carry a balance: 24% annual cost.

quiz.question: How long does it take to repay $5,000 at minimum payments?

details.summary: Credit cards are revolving credit instruments that let you borrow up to a set limit, repay monthly, and borrow again. The card issuer profits from interest on carried balances, interchange fees from merchants, and annual card fees.
details.whyItMatters: Credit cards are the most common form of consumer credit and the primary way most people build or destroy their credit scores. Understanding how issuers profit reveals why minimum payments are designed to maximize interest income.
takeaways: Revolving credit lets you borrow, repay, and borrow again up to your limit
Average credit card APR exceeds 20 percent on carried balances
Minimum payments are calculated to maximize long-term interest charges

faq.question: Why are credit card interest rates so high?
faq.answer: Credit cards are unsecured debt with no collateral. The lender cannot seize assets if you default. High interest rates compensate for this risk, plus the cost of rewards programs that are funded by interest from borrowers who carry balances.

faq.question: How does only paying the minimum hurt you?
faq.answer: Minimum payments, often 1 to 3 percent of the balance, are designed to keep you in debt as long as possible. A $5,000 balance at 20 percent APR paid at the minimum would take over 25 years to repay and cost over $8,000 in interest.
